response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness and structural contrast between author source and closed FCSTM. Key findings: (1) NL1-CARDINALITY-1 requires exactly 3 concurrent regions; the closed model text shows 4 declared PlantUML concurrent regions (region 0 with no states/transitions, plus regions 1-3 for F/R/P), so I bind the owner and mark the domain, leaving count comparison to the deterministic frontier. (2) NL2-INITIALENTRY-1 requires the collision-avoidance sub-machine itself to be entered from its enclosing scope on the three collision events; the closed model's root-level initial edge targets only 'UnspecifiedInitial', never Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode, so the owner-local entry from root/enclosing scope to the sub-machine is missing -- a clear S2-type absent-edge candidate. (3) NL3-REGIONSTRUCTURE-1 requires orthogonal regions permitting concurrent, independent activation; the closed model does declare 4 PlantUML-derived regions with F/R/P each having its own conditional initial edge (not an unconditional/default entry), and structurally the regions exist but the whole composite is unreachable from root, undermining the required concurrent-activation structure at the owner-entry level -- this is better captured via the initial-entry defect already raised in NL2, so no separate region_structure candidate is needed here since the structural declaration itself (4 declared regions with per-region initial edges) is present; however the composite's own initial pseudostate lacks an unconditional child target as an owner-local anomaly. I therefore treat NL3-REGIONSTRUCTURE-1 as satisfied at the declaration level (regions exist) and omit it. (4) NL3-STATEACTION-1 requires that active regions can concurrently perform distinct control actions; no state action/effect content exists anywhere in the closed model (all transitions have empty effects/actions), so this is a predicate-null W1 gap for the required progress/action semantics, bound to the composite and its three child regions as the exact carriers lacking action content. I also derive one additional contract for the sub-machine's own malformed/absent default-entry structure discovered only through cross-view closure: the enclosing root scope's default initial edge goes to a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial placeholder instead of the required Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode sub-machine, which is the same underlying fact as NL2 but I keep it as one candidate against NL2 rather than duplicating.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement quote; fcstm_model.text root block; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_from_initial=false for Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode; verify_facts refuted reachability check; exact_source_inventory transition inventory.
decisions.reason: The NL clause 'This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected' requires a root-owned entry edge into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode. The exact closed-model inventory shows the sole root-level initial transition (transition:line:19) targets a synthetic placeholder UnspecifiedInitial, never Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode, and no edge in the 7-transition inventory has that composite as target from the root scope. This is a genuine negative-inventory fact establishing the violation. The nested [*]->F/R/P edges are a competent alternative reading only insofar as they carry the correct collision_detected trigger and could be seen by a looser reading as realizing the 'becomes active on detection' intent structurally, but they are owned by the composite's own internal region scope, not the enclosing/root scope required by the strict owner-scoped rule; this alternative is genuinely compatible with the same facts (owner-scope ambiguity between whether NL2's obligation targets only the outermost owner edge or can be discharged by owner-local edges within the sub-machine once some future outer edge reaches it), so it survives as an undercutting reading rather than fully closing the issue.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL2 requires an enclosing/root-scope entry edge into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode triggered by a collision-detection event so the sub-machine becomes active on detection.

decisions.basis: NL3 requirement quote; inspection_equivalent_facts transition effects/guard fields for line:12-17; reference_inspection_facts.metrics.abstract_action_inventory empty.
decisions.reason: NL3 states 'The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls,' implying each region performs a distinct action. The exact closed model shows every transition tr_0001..tr_0006 (lines 12-17) has an empty effects list and the abstract_action_inventory metric is empty, so no action content exists anywhere to represent these controls. This establishes the property gap. However, the NL text is generic and does not name an exact lifecycle phase (entry/do/exit) or exact action label, so whether 'activation' must be represented by an explicit action field (as opposed to being represented purely by state identity/region membership, i.e., simply being in state F, R, or P is the 'activation') remains a competent alternative reading compatible with the same empty-effects facts; this reading is not conclusively excluded by the dossier.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL3 requires the orthogonal regions (F,R,P) of the active collision-avoidance mode to be able to concurrently activate distinct collision-avoidance control actions.

arguments.basis: Adjudicated 11 obligations for pair 0017 using the supplied NL contract text, canonical PlantUML/FCSTM source, closed FCSTM model text, inspection-equivalent facts, verify_facts, and receipts contained in each obligation dossier.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement quote; fcstm_model.text root block; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_from_initial=false for Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode; verify_facts refuted reachability check; exact_source_inventory transition inventory.
decisions.reason: The NL clause 'This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected' requires a root-owned entry edge into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode. The exact closed-model inventory shows the sole root-level initial transition (transition:line:19) targets a synthetic placeholder UnspecifiedInitial, never Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode, and no edge in the 7-transition inventory has that composite as target from the root scope. This is a genuine negative-inventory fact establishing the violation. The nested [*]->F/R/P edges are a competent alternative reading only insofar as they carry the correct collision_detected trigger and could be seen by a looser reading as realizing the 'becomes active on detection' intent structurally, but they are owned by the composite's own internal region scope, not the enclosing/root scope required by the strict owner-scoped rule; this alternative is genuinely compatible with the same facts (owner-scope ambiguity between whether NL2's obligation targets only the outermost owner edge or can be discharged by owner-local edges within the sub-machine once some future outer edge reaches it), so it survives as an undercutting reading rather than fully closing the issue.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL2 requires an enclosing/root-scope entry edge into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode triggered by a collision-detection event so the sub-machine becomes active on detection.

decisions.basis: NL3 requirement quote; inspection_equivalent_facts transition effects/guard fields for line:12-17; reference_inspection_facts.metrics.abstract_action_inventory empty.
decisions.reason: NL3 states 'The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls,' implying each region performs a distinct action. The exact closed model shows every transition tr_0001..tr_0006 (lines 12-17) has an empty effects list and the abstract_action_inventory metric is empty, so no action content exists anywhere to represent these controls. This establishes the property gap. However, the NL text is generic and does not name an exact lifecycle phase (entry/do/exit) or exact action label, so whether 'activation' must be represented by an explicit action field (as opposed to being represented purely by state identity/region membership, i.e., simply being in state F, R, or P is the 'activation') remains a competent alternative reading compatible with the same empty-effects facts; this reading is not conclusively excluded by the dossier.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL3 requires the orthogonal regions (F,R,P) of the active collision-avoidance mode to be able to concurrently activate distinct collision-avoidance control actions.

decisions.basis: Domain invariant UML-2.5.1-14.5.6.7; native-projection transition:line:16; S3 predicate receipt (backend fcstm_model:S3, verdict=false, counterexample).
decisions.reason: The domain invariant (UML-2.5.1-14.5.6.7) requires outgoing transitions from an initial pseudostate to have no trigger/guard. The exact native FCSTM projection shows transition:line:16 has triggers=['collision_detected'], directly violating the invariant; the S3 backend executed and returned verdict=false with counterexample expected=[] observed=['collision_detected']. There is no competent alternative reading of this exact structural invariant applied to this exact identified carrier; the dossier's own strongest_rebuttal (that only the exact native initial carrier is evaluated) is not an alternative reading but a scoping confirmation that supports the violation, not a defeater.
decisions.violated_obligation: Frozen UML initial-pseudostate invariant requires transition:line:16 ([*] -> P) to carry neither trigger nor guard.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement quote; fcstm_model text root scope; inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL; verify_facts refuted reachability.
decisions.reason: This dossier restates the same NL2 owner-scoped initial-entry defect for the exact root scope/UnspecifiedInitial/Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode triple: the only root-owned initial edge (line:19) targets the synthetic placeholder UnspecifiedInitial, which itself is a LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING dead end, and no edge reaches the composite from root, confirmed by inspection diagnostics and the refuted verify_facts reachability check. This is a genuine negative-inventory violation reading. As with i0, the alternative reading that the internal [*]->F/R/P edges (correctly triggered by collision_detected) might be read loosely as discharging the sub-machine's 'activation on detection' intent survives as a competent but non-conclusive undercutting alternative, since it is compatible with the same exact facts even though it does not satisfy the strict owner-scoped rule.
decisions.violated_obligation: An owner-local initial pseudostate edge from the enclosing root scope must enter Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode so detection events activate the sub-machine.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement quote; inspection_equivalent_facts states reachable_from_initial=false and unreachable_state_count=7; verify_facts refuted reachability check for state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5.
decisions.reason: NL2's activation clause presupposes the sub-machine can actually be entered from root. The exact deterministic reachability facts mark Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode and all descendants as reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts explicitly refutes the reachability check for state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5; only 2 of 9 declared states are reachable. Although the G1 predicate plan lacks a supported executable backend here (receipt verdict=unknown, backend=none), this is a W-boundary execution-availability issue, not a semantic ambiguity: the finite deterministic inventory already establishes the negative reachability fact via inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts. The dossier's own strongest_rebuttal only describes a hypothetical future repair, not a present competent alternative reading of the current closed model, so it is not a surviving defeater; it is defeated by the exact current facts.
decisions.violated_obligation: Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode must be reachable from the top-level root so activation-on-detection can occur.

decisions.basis: NL2 requirement quote; inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE; verify_facts refuted event-consumer check.
decisions.reason: NL2 requires an operational response to detection events. decisions.basis: NL3 requirement quote; fcstm_model.text region declarations; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts refuted reachability.

issues.observed: The complete closed transition inventory shows only one root-scope initial edge: [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:19), a compiler-owned synthetic placeholder with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING). No edge from the root or UnspecifiedInitial reaches Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode; the composite and its F/R/P children are all marked STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL and reachability-refuted.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the enclosing scope to activate the sub-machine on detection; the exact root-owned initial edge instead targets a synthetic placeholder with no continuation, so the required owner-local entry into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode is absent from the complete inventory.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the three inner [*] -> F/R/P edges (lines 12/14/16) inside Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode already realize event-triggered entry semantics for the sub-machine's substates; however these are owned by the composite's own regions, not by the enclosing root scope, and per the strict owner-scoped initial-entry rule they cannot satisfy a root-owned entry obligation into the composite itself, especially since the composite is never reached from root in the first place.
issues.title: No enclosing-scope initial edge enters the collision-avoidance sub-machine; root only reaches a synthetic placeholder

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states entries for Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode/F/R/P (reachable_from_initial=false) and metrics.unreachable_state_count=7; verify_facts.checks reachability entries refuted for state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5, F/R/P, and FinalWait* states.
issues.expected: Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode must be reachable from the top-level root so that activation on detection events can actually occur.
issues.observed: Deterministic reachability facts mark Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode and every descendant (F, R, P, FinalWaittr_0002/0004/0006) as reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts explicitly refutes reachability:state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5; only 2 of 9 declared states (root and UnspecifiedInitial) are reachable.
issues.reason: Root reachability to the sub-machine is a distinct behavioral-consequence property from the narrower initial-entry pseudostate-edge obligation: even a locally well-formed initial edge inside the composite cannot discharge this global reachability requirement, and the deterministic facts show the composite is completely cut off from root.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If a future repair adds a root edge directly into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode or redirects UnspecifiedInitial's outgoing edge there, reachability would close without needing any other change; this shows the defect is a single missing edge rather than a deep structural break, but it remains an actual violation in the current closed model.
issues.title: The collision-avoidance sub-machine is unreachable from the root of the closed FCSTM

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers (collision_detected declared_ref=event:collision_detected:line:2, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE line=null referring transitions line:12/14/16; verify_facts.checks check_id=event-consumer:collision_detected status=refuted.
issues.expected: At least one of the three collision_detected-triggered transitions ([*] -> F, [*] -> R, [*] -> P inside Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode) must be reachable so detecting a collision actually activates sub-machine behavior.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for collision_detected lists consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:12,14,16] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_state_refs=[]; the diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE is raised; verify_facts.checks event-consumer:collision_detected is refuted.
issues.reason: NL2's 'becomes active when ... is detected' is an operational response obligation; declared-but-unreachable consumers cannot discharge it, and the deterministic facts show this exact gap for all three detection alternatives simultaneously.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The three consumer transitions are declared and syntactically well-formed with correct triggers, so a purely declarative reading of 'consumes the event' would be satisfied; however NL2's activation semantics requires an operational response, and the deterministic reachable-consumer facts explicitly show no consumer is currently reachable from root.
issues.title: The collision_detected event has declared consumers but zero reachable consumers

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text PlantUML concurrent region annotations listing 3 regions with F/R/P plus separators; inspection_equivalent_facts.states Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.checks reachability refuted for the composite and its children.
issues.expected: The three orthogonal regions of Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode must permit actual simultaneous, independent activation of distinct collision avoidance controls (F, R, P) once the mode is active.
issues.observed: The closed model declares exactly three concurrent regions (region 1: F/tr_0001/tr_0002; region 2: R/tr_0003/tr_0004; region 3: P/tr_0005/tr_0006) which is structurally correct, but the entire composite Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode is unreachable from root, so the orthogonal regions can never actually be entered or concurrently activated in any execution.
issues.reason: Although the static partition count and independence are correct, the behavior-consequence lens must flag that this structural guarantee has no operational effect because the composite housing the regions is never reached, so the 'allow for concurrent activation' consequence stated in NL3 cannot occur in any execution of the closed model.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The region_structure obligation, read narrowly as static topology (three orthogonal partitions exist), is fully satisfied by the closed model's declared region projection, independent of reachability; the unreachability defect belongs to the separate reachability contract/candidate rather than to region_structure itself.
issues.title: Orthogonal regions exist structurally but are never operationally reachable to permit the required concurrent activation
